Hatching of surfaces and meshes

Source: R/hatch-3d.R
hatch_3d.Rd

hatch_3d() draws a surface or mesh layer's tone as hatching, passed as the layer's hatch argument. With space = "model" the strokes are the intersections of the triangles with parallel planes: angle turns the planes' normal in the panel's x-y plane from the x axis, so angle = 0 gives lines of constant x (the iso-parameter lines of a grid surface) and angle = 90 lines of constant y; cross = TRUE adds the perpendicular family. The strokes are lines of the scene, hidden by nearer surfaces like any other line, so in vector output they are exact; with a white fill, or with backend_3d("plotter"), the figure is drawn with lines only.

Usage

hatch_3d(
  angle = 45,
  spacing = NULL,
  cross = TRUE,
  tone = TRUE,
  space = c("model", "screen"),
  colour = "black",
  linewidth = 0.25,
  alpha = 1
)

Arguments

angle

Angle in degrees of the first family.

spacing

Distance between lines: a fraction of the panel box side for space = "model", mm for "screen". NULL takes 0.015 and 1.2.

cross

Whether the dark tones add the perpendicular family.

tone

Whether line density follows the shading.

space

"model" or "screen".

colour, linewidth, alpha

Stroke of the lines.

Value

A hatching specification for the hatch argument of geom_surface_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and the surface stats.

Details

With tone = TRUE the density follows the shading: every face is lit (as a white face of the layer's material) and its darkness, one minus the encoded grey, selects how many lines it keeps, from every fourth line in light tones to every line, then the cross family, in dark tones. The lines kept at one tone contain those kept at every lighter tone, the nesting of the tonal art maps of Praun et al. (2001), so strokes run on unbroken where the tone changes. Without a light every line of the first family is drawn.

With space = "screen" the faces get a hatch pattern in device space instead (a grid::pattern() fill per tone band, as in Murrell's vector pattern fills): lines spacing mm apart, twice as far in light faces, crossed in dark ones. It needs a device with pattern fills (ragg, svg, cairo_pdf, pdf) and is drawn by the vector backend.

References

Praun, Hoppe, Webb, Finkelstein (2001). Real-time hatching. SIGGRAPH 2001, 581-586. doi:10.1145/383259.383328

Hertzmann and Zorin (2000). Illustrating smooth surfaces. SIGGRAPH 2000, 517-526. doi:10.1145/344779.345074

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 30), y = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 30))
d$z <- with(d, exp(-(x^2 + y^2)))
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z))
p + geom_surface_3d(fill = "white", colour = NA, hatch = hatch_3d(angle = 0)) + coord_3d()
p + geom_surface_3d(fill = "white", colour = NA, hatch = hatch_3d(space = "screen")) + coord_3d()
